hypotheses.title: ABC44 Shortens Lifespan in C. elegans
hypotheses.claim: Exposure to ABC44 reduces lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans. The compound acts as a detrimental intervention in this organism.
hypotheses.rationale: Exogenous compounds can disrupt conserved cellular processes such as mitochondrial function or proteostasis, and such disruption generally accelerates aging in C. elegans.
hypotheses.prediction: Worms cultured with ABC44 will show a statistically significant decrease in mean and maximum lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Synchronize worm populations, raise them on ABC44-supplemented and control plates, and score survival daily until all animals die, comparing lifespan curves by log-rank analysis.

hypotheses.title: Cranberry Extract Shortens Lifespan in C. elegans
hypotheses.claim: Exposure to cranberry extract reduces lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans. The extract acts as a detrimental intervention in this organism.
hypotheses.rationale: Plant extracts contain bioactive molecules that can impose metabolic or oxidative stress, and stress above a tolerable threshold typically shortens lifespan in C. elegans.
hypotheses.prediction: Worms cultured with cranberry extract will show a statistically significant decrease in mean and maximum lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Synchronize worm populations, raise them on cranberry extract-supplemented and control plates, and score survival daily until all animals die, comparing lifespan curves by log-rank analysis.

hypotheses.title: ABC44 Extends Lifespan via DAF-2 Activation
hypotheses.claim: Exposure to ABC44 extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans by activating the insulin/IGF-1 receptor DAF-2. The compound acts through this specific signaling receptor.
hypotheses.rationale: The insulin/IGF-1 pathway is a central regulator of aging in C. elegans, and modulation of DAF-2 activity can alter downstream FOXO signaling and lifespan.
hypotheses.prediction: Worms cultured with ABC44 will live longer than controls, and the extension will be abolished in daf-2 loss-of-function mutants.
hypotheses.experiment: Compare lifespan of wild-type and daf-2 mutant worms on ABC44-supplemented and control plates, testing whether ABC44 fails to extend lifespan when DAF-2 function is absent.

hypotheses.claim: Exposure to cranberry extract extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans. The extract acts as a beneficial intervention in this organism.
hypotheses.rationale: Plant-derived polyphenols can activate endogenous stress-response pathways, and mild activation of such pathways is a common route to lifespan extension in C. elegans.
hypotheses.prediction: Worms cultured with cranberry extract will show a statistically significant increase in mean and maximum lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Synchronize worm populations, raise them on cranberry extract-supplemented and control plates, and score survival daily until all animals die, comparing lifespan curves by log-rank analysis.
